_comment: How the game client presents the table: timings, camera shots, jumps, dice. Look and feel only: the rules never read this file. Lengths are in road spaces unless named otherwise, times in seconds at normal speed, angles in radians unless named otherwise. Each block names the module of src/app/ that reads it.

beats._module: beats.ts: how long each beat of the rules lasts before the next one
beats._settle: After the last beat the table must come to rest (cars parked, dice landed, effects and the worm over) before the next choice or the end of the game; settle_max_s: the longest wait, in seconds of real time, in case something never stops.

drive._module: cars.ts: cars driving between spaces (world units per second, radians per second, radians)

route._module: route.ts: how a car drives forward through spaces, as a driver would (asked by the user, 2026-11-19). It sets off and arrives along its lane (the Big Rig may stop at a slant). World units per second (top, crawl: the speed it starts from and stops at), per second squared (accel, brake, grip: the sideways pull that caps the speed in a bend); tangent: how far the curve keeps its heading at each space, as a share of the leg.

trail._module: trail.ts: what a moving car throws up behind it (asked by the user, 2026-11-19). looks: soft sprites (colour; rate: grains per second at full speed; size: from and to, in spaces; life in seconds; alpha; up: how fast it rises; grav: gravity, negative rises; spread; glow: added light). ground: the looks each terrain throws up (R road, o off-road sand, X impassable, P ramp, S salt flat, M mud, G toxic slime, D desert glass, F fire). liquids: mud and slime are thrown as wet drops that fly in arcs, land and lie as splats (size: radius from and to, in spaces; up: upward speed from and to; kick: share of the car's speed thrown back; gravity; gloss: roughness of the wet surface, lower is shinier; glow: how much the slime shines by itself; splat: the splat's radius as a multiple of the drop's).

jump._module: cars.ts: the ramp jump (Carnage at Devil's Run)

dice_throw._module: rolls.ts, view/dice-throw.ts: how an FX die is thrown. Lengths in dice (1 = the die's width). seconds: how long the throw lasts; peak: height of the first flight; bounce: heights of the bounces; roll_quarters: quarter turns tumbled on the ground at the end, at most; spin: turning in the air, times the rolling rate; wobble: extra turns off axis at the start; ease: how much it slows down; reach: how far from the landing spot a piece may be struck; detour: how much longer the way by that piece may be; hit_height: how high it strikes; toss_turns: turns when thrown again where it lies; car_r, rock_r: radius of the pieces it bounces off, in road spaces; same_action: a roll farther than this from the last one (road spaces) is a new action, and the dice out go home first; farthest: how far from the action a die may land when nothing nearer is clear (road spaces); clear: [across, along the view] the box around a vehicle where no die lands, so neither hides the other (road spaces).

director._director2: shots.ts, the new director (design/gdd/camera-director.md). hold: seconds in which a new event joins the shot being taken; refresh: seconds between two looks at the interface; floor: the camera's lowest height above the tile. subject: radius of what a shot must show (a car, a car in close-up, a slam with the six spaces around it, a chopper's target and how high above it the chopper is, a die). blocker: radius and height of what can hide the action. shots: for each event the ways of filming it, the first being the one meant for it: yaw and elev in DEGREES (yaw 0 behind the action, 90 side on; both sides are tried), fill the share of the free part of the screen the subjects take, near the closest the camera comes, orbit degrees per second around the subjects.
director._merge: merge: road spaces; a new event (or a die rolled) joins the shot being taken only when it is this close to what the shot shows, else the camera cuts to it (asked by the user, 2026-11-19: the camera stayed on one action while dice were rolled for another). shots.roll: how a die rolled for an action is filmed, with that action's space.
director._worm: subject.worm: the radius of the sand worm's show (the worm out of the ground and the car thrown over its open mouth), worm_up how high above the ground its middle is; shots.worm: how it is filmed.

chase._module: chase.ts: the view from behind a car (fov in degrees, lift a share of the window's height, follow per second); enabled false hides it (user, 2026-11-17: to be reworked)

chase_dice._module: tableDice.ts: the dice lying by the car in the chase view (every in seconds, slide per second)

map_view._module: mapView.ts: framing the map (side in screen units, high in world units, gap in pixels; swap in seconds)

replay._module: replay.ts: the instant replay (speed a share of normal, before/after in beats, camera offset in world units)

sand_worm._module: app/worm.ts: the sand worm swallowing a car. seconds: the whole show; width: the body's width in road spaces; up: the lean (radians) that turns its mouth to the sky under the car; gape, shut: how far the jaws open and close (radians); sway: how far it leans about after swallowing (radians); mound: how high the ground swells under the car before it bursts (road spaces); launch: how high the car flies over the open mouth (road spaces); dust: grains of dust in the burst (half on low quality); shares of the show: quake (the ground swells, then bursts), rise (the worm is out), gulp (the car falls into the jaws and they shut), dive (it starts to go down).

bubbles._module: hud.ts: the players' bubbles in turn order; seconds a bubble takes to slide to its new place when the order changes (the roll for the first player, a new round).

turn_splash._module: app/turnsplash.ts: the "Tocca a..." band at the start of a person's turn; seconds before it goes by itself (a click or a key closes it sooner).

shrapnel._module: shrapnel.ts: the Shrapnel damage token, a jagged piece of sheet metal torn off the damaged car flies the way the direction die says; it hits the first vehicle in that line or flies off the road (asked by the user, 2026-11-19)
shrapnel._units: windup, after, min_flight: seconds; speed: road spaces per second; apex, height, hit_height, size: road spaces; spin: radians per second; bits: smaller fragments flying with it; metal: how metallic it looks (0-1); glint: how much of its own colour it gives off, so it reads in the shade

salvo._module: salvo.ts: the Big Rig's Missile Launcher, a rocket salvo on the spaces it strikes (asked by the user, 2026-11-18)
salvo._units: seconds: the beat's length; per_space: rockets on each space; stagger: seconds between two launches; flight: seconds in the air; apex: height of the arc in road spaces; mark: seconds the struck spaces stay lit after the last hit

wreckage._module: wreckage.ts: a destroyed car goes to pieces and leaves a charred heap on its last space; a car falls into a pit trap, then the pit blows up (asked by the user, 2026-11-19)
wreckage._units: grid: chunks along the car's length, height and width; char: colour kept by the charred chunks (0 black, 1 as they were); glow: how hot they glow at first; cool: seconds to cool down; heap: radius of the heap in road spaces; flight: shortest and longest flight of a chunk in seconds; settle: seconds after the last landing; lift: height of the throw in road spaces; spin: radians per second of tumbling; bounce: height of the bounce in road spaces; ground: height of a chunk's middle over the table in road spaces; flames: size of the flames left on the heap in road spaces; pit: roll seconds onto the hole, drop seconds into it, after seconds of the blast, depth in road spaces, tip radians nose down, blast size (1 = a car blowing up)
